newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya's Moi says opposition out to create chaos.
newsitem.headline: Kenya's Moi says opposition out to create chaos.

text.p: President Daniel arap Moi, under pressure from Kenya's opposition for constitutional reform, on Monday accused his opponents of creating chaos and warned he would crack down on acts of lawlessness.

State radio quoted the veteran politician, aged 73 and in power for 19 years, as condemning last Friday's political violence in which four people were killed after a national strike called by pro-reform activists.
"President Moi observed that the recent events had clearly demonstrated that the opposition were not genuine in their demands for reforms, but are only interested in creating chaos," the radio said.
"The government will continue to act tough against the perpetrators of crime," Moi said, adding that he fully supported the police in their measures to combat crime.
Four people, two of them policemen, were killed when a strike called by the opposition-backed National Convention Executive Council (NCEC) on Friday turned violent.
The strike call attracted only limited support, but unruly mobs in the capital Nairobi looted shops and set fire to trees in the city centre.
The strike put further pressure on Moi's government, whose reluctance to fight graft led to the cancellation of a $205 million International Monetary Fund (IMF) aid package on July 31.
The shilling, battered by the IMF decision, took a further beating on Monday on renewed demand for the dollar from foreign investors pulling out of a nervous market, dealers said.
The shilling closed at a commercial mean rate of 70 to the dollar from Monday's opening at 68.87 -- a loss of 1.64 percent.
Some commercial banks quoted rates of up to 72 to the dollar.

The crisis in Kenya's money market worsened on Monday after weekend reports in local dailies that the World Bank was contemplating cutting off aid for vital programmes such as road building and repairs.
The privately owned Sunday Nation said the bank had delayed disbursement of up to $71 million in Structural Adjustment Credit and other projects before the IMF decision.

Attorney-General Amos Wako has published a bill providing for minimal constitutional reforms and another for a commission to carry out a full review of the constitution, expected in parliament within days.

Moi, who must hold presidential and parliamentary elections later this year has also been hit by industrial unrest from air traffic controllers who last week nearly brought flights in and out of the country to a standstill.
